title: A finite purely inseparable extension descends along a field extension
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields ($L$ a field extension of $K$ [def-pc-field-extension]) and let $B$ be a commutative $K$-algebra. Regard $L\otimes_KB$ as an $L$-algebra via $l\mapsto l\otimes1$. If $L\otimes_KB$ is a field and, via this map, a finite purely inseparable field extension of $L$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], then $B$ is a field, the structure map $K\to B$ makes $B$ a finite purely inseparable field extension of $K$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and $\dim_KB=\dim_L(L\otimes_KB)$.

source.place: Implicit in the proof of Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202), where $k_i'$ is asserted to be a finite purely inseparable field extension of $k_i$ without argument; definition of purely inseparable: Fields, Definition Tag 09HE (fields.tex). Intended argument (agent): choose a $K$-basis of $L$ containing $1$ and a $K$-basis $(b_\lambda)$ of $B$ containing $1$; then $(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ is an $L$-basis of $L\otimes_KB$, so $\dim_KB=\dim_L(L\otimes_KB)<\infty$, and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$ is injective; hence $B$ is a domain finite over $K$, so a field; if $\beta\in B$ has $(1\otimes\beta)^q=l\otimes1$ ($q$ a power of the characteristic exponent), comparing coordinates in the basis $(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ gives $\beta^q\in K$; in characteristic $0$, $\dim=1$ gives $B=K$.

proof.text: Step 1: Module.finrank_baseChange gives dim_K B = dim_L (L tensor_K B). The latter is positive since the tensor product is a nontrivial finite-dimensional L-vector space. Module.finite_of_finrank_pos then gives Module.Finite K B. This uses Mathlib directly and does not choose a basis of B through 1.

Step 2: Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_injective, using flatness over the field K and injectivity of K to L, embeds B in L tensor_K B. Transfer IsDomain along this injection; fieldOfFiniteDimensional K B then gives IsField B.

Step 3: Choose a K-linear functional f on L with f(1)=1, by Module.Projective.exists_dual_eq_one (vector spaces are free and hence projective). Tensor f with the identity on B and compose with TensorProduct.lid K B. The resulting K-linear map pi sends l tensor b to f(l) times b. This is a fully proved Mathlib existence theorem, not data chosen from an unproved theorem.

Step 4: Let q be the exponential characteristic of K. Injectivity of K to L gives ExpChar L q. For each b in B, IsPurelyInseparable.pow_mem gives n and l such that (1 tensor b)^(q^n)=l tensor 1. The ring homomorphism includeRight identifies the left side with 1 tensor b^(q^n). Applying pi from step 3 gives b^(q^n)=f(l) times 1, hence membership in the image of K. Apply isPurelyInseparable_iff_pow_mem K q. This simultaneously treats positive characteristic and characteristic zero (q=1). Combine with steps 1 and 2.
